findings.claim: As drawn, A and B lock the shade on. In both, the crown's Ø84 part (A's hidden skirt, B's first tier) sits 0.5 mm above the collar's top and over the collar's wall. To come off or go on, the shade has to rise at least 7.5 mm for its bayonet, so it cannot be fitted or swapped by hand. Covering the PEEK ring is what causes this: the ring (Ø81.6) sits inside the collar's Ø82 bore, so any fixture part wide enough to cover it from above also hangs over the collar. Today's Ø80 crown sits inside the bore and the collar slides up around it.

findings.claim: A's offered fix cannot work. A Ø90 skirt flush with the clamp ring's top covers even more of the collar's top (r 41 to 45) and blocks the lift further. 'Above the pins, so the bayonet still clears' confuses which parts move: the skirt and the pins are both on the fixture, and the collar is what has to pass.
